instruction: I want to use a dark color scheme in my terminal. Set the terminal to use the 'Tango dark' built-in color scheme permanently so it persists after reboot.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(1); pyautogui.write('gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.Legacy.Profile:/org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/:$(gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.ProfilesList default | tr -d "'")/ use-theme-colors'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.explanation: Task requires permanently setting terminal to use custom color scheme (not theme colors). Evaluator opens new terminal and checks use-theme-colors setting using gsettings, expecting 'false' which indicates custom colors are being used. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_terminal_output getter.
metadata.similarity_to_original: high - same pattern of OS terminal configuration that persists across reboots

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification: Instruction requires setting 'Tango dark' color scheme specifically, but evaluator only checks if use-theme-colors is false
Missing critical check: Evaluator does not verify which color scheme/profile is actually active - use-theme-colors=false only means custom colors are enabled, not that 'Tango dark' is selected
Coverage gap: The setting could pass with ANY custom color scheme configured, not necessarily 'Tango dark' as required by instruction
Logical flaw: Checking use-theme-colors=false is a necessary but insufficient condition - it's a prerequisite for custom schemes but doesn't verify the specific scheme name
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add verification for the actual color scheme name/profile - check visible-name or palette settings to confirm 'Tango dark' is active

Could use: gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.Legacy.Profile:/org/gnome/terminal/legacy/profiles:/:$(gsettings get org.gnome.Terminal.ProfilesList default | tr -d "'")/ visible-name and check for 'Tango dark'
Alternative: Check palette colors to verify they match Tango dark palette values
Consider multi-step verification: (1) use-theme-colors=false AND (2) visible-name contains 'Tango dark' OR palette matches expected values
